class.name: GodotPrismBackend
class.brief_description: A screen reader or speech engine.
class.description: A backend presents text through the user's screen reader or through a speech engine. Backends are obtained from the [code]Prism[/code] singleton, a [GodotPrismContext], and are initialized before they are returned. An instance created with [code]new()[/code] refers to no backend, and [method is_valid] returns [code]false[/code] for it. The backend is released with its last reference. Speech in progress is stopped first, if the backend supports [method stop]. Keep a reference for as long as speech should continue, for example in a member variable. Backends support different operations; [member features] reports which. An unsupported operation returns [constant PRISM_ERROR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED]. Methods that can fail return a [enum PrismError] value, described by [method GodotPrismContext.get_error_string]. Property setters and getters print errors instead, and getters then return the value documented for the property. A backend must not be used from more than one thread at a time. Backends returned by [method GodotPrismContext.acquire] share an instance, and this applies to all of them. Use [method output] for messages to the user; it reaches both speech and braille. The [member rate], [member pitch], and [member volume] of screen reader backends cannot be changed.

method.name: braille
method.description: Shows [param text] on the user's braille display, according to the screen reader's braille settings. Braille output does not affect speech. Returns [constant PRISM_ERROR_INVALID_PARAM] if [param text] is empty, and [constant PRISM_ERROR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED] if the backend does not support braille, as no speech engine does. Some backends succeed when no display is connected and others fail, so the result does not indicate whether a display is present.

method.name: find_voice
method.description: Returns the index of the first voice whose name contains [param pattern], ignoring case, or [code]-1[/code] if [param pattern] is empty or no voice matches.

method.name: find_voice_by_language
method.description: Returns the index of the first voice whose language begins with [param prefix], ignoring case, or [code]-1[/code] if [param prefix] is empty or no voice matches. [code]"en"[/code] matches [code]"en-US"[/code] and [code]"en-GB"[/code].

method.name: get_voice_language
method.description: Returns the language of the voice at [param index], usually a BCP 47 tag such as [code]"en-US"[/code]. Returns an empty [String] if the backend does not support voices, [param index] is out of range, or the query fails.

method.name: get_voice_name
method.description: Returns the name of the voice at [param index], such as [code]"Microsoft David"[/code]. Returns an empty [String] if the backend does not support voices, [param index] is out of range, or the query fails.

method.name: get_voices
method.description: Returns a [Dictionary] for each voice, in index order, with the keys [code]"index"[/code], [code]"name"[/code], and [code]"language"[/code]. Returns an empty array if the backend does not support voices.

method.name: has_feature
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the backend has every feature in [param flag]. The backend is queried on each call. [codeblock] if backend.has_feature(GodotPrismBackend.PRISM_BACKEND_SUPPORTS_IS_SPEAKING): print(backend.speaking) [/codeblock]

method.name: is_valid
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the object refers to a backend. A backend that failed to initialize is valid; its methods return [constant PRISM_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED].

method.name: output
method.description: Presents [param text] through speech and braille. A screen reader backend speaks the text and shows it on the braille display; a speech engine speaks it. [param interrupt] has the same meaning as for [method speak]. Returns [constant PRISM_ERROR_INVALID_PARAM] if [param text] is empty. May return [constant PRISM_OK] when one of speech and braille fails.

method.name: pause
method.description: Pauses speech. Queued speech is kept, and [method resume] continues from the same position. While paused, [member speaking] is [code]false[/code]. Returns [constant PRISM_ERROR_NOT_SPEAKING] if no speech is in progress, [constant PRISM_ERROR_ALREADY_PAUSED] if speech is already paused, and [constant PRISM_ERROR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED] if the backend does not support pausing.

method.name: refresh_voices
method.description: Reloads the list of voices from the system. Voices installed while the project runs appear only after a refresh. Voice indices may change, so a stored choice of voice should be identified by name, for example with [method find_voice]. Returns [constant PRISM_ERROR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED] if the backend does not support voices, as no screen reader does.

method.name: resume
method.description: Resumes speech paused by [method pause]. Returns [constant PRISM_ERROR_NOT_PAUSED] if speech is not paused, including after [method stop], and [constant PRISM_ERROR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED] if the backend does not support resuming.

method.name: speak
method.description: Speaks [param text] with the current voice, rate, pitch, and volume. Depending on the backend, returns when speech starts or when it ends. If [param interrupt] is [code]true[/code], speech in progress is stopped and queued speech is discarded first. If [code]false[/code], most backends queue the text; some mix it with speech in progress, and screen readers may apply their own setting. Returns [constant PRISM_ERROR_INVALID_PARAM] if [param text] is empty, [constant PRISM_ERROR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED] if the backend does not support speech, and [constant PRISM_ERROR_SPEAK_FAILURE] if synthesis fails. Some backends limit the length of text, so long text should be divided. [codeblock] var err := backend.speak("Hello from Prism.", true) if err != GodotPrismBackend.PRISM_OK: push_error("Speech failed: %s" % Prism.get_error_string(err)) [/codeblock]

method.name: speak_to_memory
method.description: Synthesizes [param text] and calls [param callback] once with the audio: a [PackedFloat32Array] of interleaved samples from [code]-1.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code], the number of channels, and the sample rate in hertz. [param callback] is called on the calling thread before the method returns, and is not called if synthesis fails. The method may take noticeable time for long text. Returns [constant PRISM_ERROR_INVALID_PARAM] if [param text] is empty or [param callback] is invalid, and [constant PRISM_ERROR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED] if the backend does not support synthesis to memory, as no screen reader does. See also [method speak_to_stream].

method.name: speak_to_stream
method.description: Synthesizes [param text] and returns the audio as a 16-bit [AudioStreamWAV], which can be played through an [AudioStreamPlayer] or a positional player. Returns [code]null[/code] if [param text] is empty, the backend does not support synthesis to memory, synthesis fails, or no audio is produced. Failures other than empty text and empty audio are printed. The stream is stereo if the backend produces more than one channel; more than two channels are not represented correctly. [codeblock] var stream := backend.speak_to_stream("Behind you.") if stream != null: $AudioStreamPlayer3D.stream = stream $AudioStreamPlayer3D.play() [/codeblock]

method.name: stop
method.description: Stops speech and discards queued speech. A screen reader backend stops only speech it produced. Returns [constant PRISM_ERROR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED] if the backend does not support stopping. Some backends return [constant PRISM_ERROR_NOT_SPEAKING] if no speech is in progress; most return [constant PRISM_OK].

members.member: The bit depth of the speech engine's native audio, commonly 8 or 16. [method speak_to_memory] always delivers floating-point samples. [code]-1[/code] if the backend does not support synthesis to memory or the query fails.
The number of channels in synthesized audio, usually [code]1[/code]. It depends on the [member voice]. [code]-1[/code] if the backend does not support synthesis to memory or the query fails.
The backend's [enum PrismBackendFeature] flags. The backend is queried each time the property is read.
The name of the backend, such as [code]"NVDA"[/code].

The pitch of speech, from [code]0.0[/code] (lowest) to [code]1.0[/code] (highest). [code]0.5[/code] is the backend's default. A new value applies to subsequent speech. Not supported by screen readers, or by speech engines whose voices have a fixed pitch. Reads [code]0.5[/code] if unsupported and [code]NAN[/code] if the query fails. Setting a value outside the range, or setting it on a backend that does not support it, prints an error.

The rate of speech, from [code]0.0[/code] (slowest) to [code]1.0[/code] (fastest). [code]0.5[/code] is always the backend's default. A new value applies to subsequent speech. Not supported by screen readers. Reads [code]0.5[/code] if unsupported and [code]NAN[/code] if the query fails. Setting a value outside the range, or setting it on a backend that does not support it, prints an error.
The sample rate of synthesized audio, in hertz. It depends on the [member voice]. [code]-1[/code] if the backend does not support synthesis to memory or the query fails.

[code]true[/code] while speech is in progress. Paused speech is not in progress. Reads [code]false[/code] if the backend cannot report its state, as most screen readers cannot, or if the query fails; check [constant PRISM_BACKEND_SUPPORTS_IS_SPEAKING] before relying on [code]false[/code].

The index of the voice used for speech, from [code]0[/code] to [member voices_count] minus one. Initially the backend's default voice. A new voice applies to subsequent speech, and may change [member channels], [member sample_rate], and [member bit_depth]. Reads [code]-1[/code] if the backend does not support voices or the query fails. Setting an index out of range, or setting it on a backend that does not support voices, prints an error.
The number of voices, as of the last [method refresh_voices]. [code]0[/code] if no voices are installed, the backend does not support voices, or the query fails.

The volume of speech, from [code]0.0[/code] (silent) to [code]1.0[/code] (loudest), independent of the system volume. [code]0.5[/code] is the backend's default. A new value applies to subsequent speech. Not supported by screen readers. Reads [code]0.5[/code] if unsupported and [code]NAN[/code] if the query fails. Setting a value outside the range, or setting it on a backend that does not support it, prints an error.
